gloss: futile effort; like talking to a wall

definitions.gloss: futile effort; pointless action; like talking to a wall; having no effect
definitions.explanation: An idiomatic expression meaning that one's efforts or words have no effect whatsoever, like trying to drive a nail into rice bran — it goes in but has no hold.

examples.japanese: {何|なに}を{言|い}っても{糠|ぬか}に{釘|くぎ}だ。
examples.english: No matter what I say, it has no effect.

examples.japanese: {注意|ちゅうい}しても{糠|ぬか}に{釘|くぎ}で、{全然|ぜんぜん}{直|なお}らない。
examples.english: Even when I warn him, it has no effect and he doesn't change at all.

examples.japanese: あの{人|ひと}に{意見|いけん}するのは{糠|ぬか}に{釘|くぎ}だから、もう{諦|あきら}めた。
examples.english: Giving that person advice is like talking to a wall, so I've given up.

notes:
A well-known Japanese proverb describing a situation where one's actions or words are completely ineffective. The image is of hammering a nail into rice bran — the nail enters easily but has no grip, making the effort pointless.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ～ても{糠|ぬか}に{釘|くぎ}だ: even if you do X, it has no effect
- {糠|ぬか}に{釘|くぎ}の{状態|じょうたい}: a state of having no effect

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {暖簾|のれん}に{腕押|うでお}し: pushing against a curtain — futile effort, same meaning
- {馬|うま}の{耳|みみ}に{念仏|ねんぶつ}: chanting sutras to a horse's ears — wasted on someone who cannot understand
- {蛙|かえる}の{面|つら}に{水|みず}: water off a frog's face — criticism that has no effect because the person doesn't care

ETYMOLOGY:
{糠|ぬか} (rice bran) is soft and powdery. A {釘|くぎ} (nail) driven into it would have no hold at all, making the effort entirely pointless.
